easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “A wise son maketh a glad father.”
Verse 4 says, “the hand of the diligent maketh rich.”
easy.q: What does the diligent hand make?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “the name of the wicked shall rot.”
easy.q: What happens to the name of the wicked?

answers: The wise son makes his father glad, while the foolish son is the heaviness of his mother
The wise son sleeps in harvest, while the foolish son gathers in summer
The wise son brings poverty, while the foolish son brings riches
medium.explanation: Verse 1 contrasts the joy caused by a wise son with the grief caused by a foolish son.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the wise son and the foolish son?

answers: He is a son that causeth shame
medium.explanation: Verse 5 calls him “a son that causeth shame.”
medium.q: What happens to the person who sleeps in harvest?

medium.explanation: Verse 2 contrasts profitless wicked wealth with righteousness that delivereth from death.
medium.q: What is the meaning of “treasures of wickedness” in context?

answers: Good results are connected with diligent action at the proper time
Rest is the path to prosperity
challenge.explanation: Verses 4–5 commend diligence and timely work.
challenge.q: What common idea appears in gathering in summer and the hand of the diligent?

answers: The righteous and wicked receive the same result
A person’s moral path affects what comes from him and how he is regarded
The passage is only about outward appearance
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 contrasts blessing connected with the just and violence associated with the wicked.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between blessings on the just and violence covering the wicked mouth?

answers: The just are remembered with blessing, while the wicked’s name decays
The just are forgotten, while the wicked are honored
Both are remembered in exactly the same way
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 says, “The memory of the just is blessed,” but the wicked’s name shall rot.
challenge.q: What change is described concerning the memory of the just and the name of the wicked?

paragraphs.title: The Power of Speech and Wisdom

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “The wise in heart will receive commandments.”
easy.q: What will the wise in heart receive?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 calls it “a well of life.”
easy.q: What is the mouth of a righteous man compared to?

medium.explanation: Verse 9 says, “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely.”
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between walking uprightly and safety?

answers: Foolish, excessive talking can lead to ruin
medium.explanation: Verses 8 and 10 connect foolish, excessive speech with falling.
medium.q: What does “a prating fool shall fall” mean in context?
How does love act in relation to sins?

answers: Both behaviors can cause sorrow or trouble
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 says the winker causeth sorrow, and the prating fool shall fall.
challenge.q: What common danger is suggested by winking with the eye and being a prating fool?

answers: They receive, find, or store wisdom and knowledge
challenge.explanation: Verses 8, 13, and 14 commend wisdom, understanding, and stored knowledge.
challenge.q: What quality is shared by the wise in heart, the understanding person, and wise men?

answers: Restraint in speech is wise, while many words can involve sin
Speaking more is always better than silence
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 says that in many words sin is not lacking, but the restrained speaker is wise.
challenge.q: What can be learned from refraining the lips and the multitude of words?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “The rich man’s wealth is his strong city.”
easy.q: What is the rich man’s wealth to him?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “The labour of the righteous tendeth to life.”
easy.q: What does the labour of the righteous tend to?

easy.explanation: Verse 22 says, “The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich.”
easy.q: What does the blessing of the LORD make?

answers: Wealth is a strong city to the rich, while poverty brings destruction to the poor
The rich suffer while the poor prosper
Both have the same kind of security
medium.explanation: Verse 15 presents wealth as protection to the rich and poverty as destruction to the poor.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the rich and the poor in verse 15?

answers: Teaching or correction that guides a person
medium.explanation: Verse 17 presents instruction as guidance on the way of life.
medium.q: What does “instruction” mean in “the way of life that keepeth instruction”?

answers: It is the way of life
medium.explanation: Verse 17 says that the person who keeps instruction is in the way of life.
medium.q: What does the passage teach about keeping instruction?

answers: The just person’s words are presented as valuable and excellent
The just person speaks only about commerce
The just person’s speech has no value
challenge.explanation: Verse 20 compares the tongue of the just to choice silver.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the tongue of the just and choice silver?

answers: Helpful, restrained speech reflects wisdom, while harmful or excessive speech can involve sin
challenge.explanation: Verses 19–21 praise restrained and nourishing speech while warning about sinful words.
challenge.q: How do these verses connect useful speech with moral responsibility?

answers: The righteous tend to life, while the wicked produce sin
The righteous produce sin, while the wicked tend to life
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 directly contrasts the labour of the righteous with the fruit of the wicked.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the fruit of the wicked and the labour of the righteous?

paragraphs.title: The Outcomes of the Righteous and the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “It is as sport to a fool to do mischief.”
easy.q: What is it like for a fool to do mischief?

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “The fear of the LORD prolongeth days.”
easy.q: What does the fear of the LORD do?

easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “the expectation of the wicked shall perish.”
easy.q: What shall happen to the expectation of the wicked?

answers: The fool delights in mischief, while the understanding man has wisdom
The understanding man delights only in riches
medium.explanation: Verse 23 contrasts the fool’s pleasure in wrongdoing with the understanding man’s wisdom.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the fool’s delight and the understanding man’s delight?

answers: The thing the wicked person fears
A place where the wicked live
medium.explanation: Verse 24 says that what the wicked fear shall come upon him.
medium.q: What does “the fear of the wicked” mean in context?

answers: The wicked pass away, while the righteous are an everlasting foundation
The righteous pass away, while the wicked remain
Both are swept away by the storm
medium.explanation: Verse 25 compares the disappearance of the wicked with the lasting foundation of the righteous.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the whirlwind and the righteous foundation?

answers: It is strength to the upright and destruction to workers of iniquity
It gives shelter only to workers of iniquity
It has no effect on anyone
challenge.explanation: Verse 29 gives opposite results for the upright and the workers of iniquity.
challenge.q: How is the way of the LORD described in relation to the upright and workers of iniquity?

answers: The fear of the LORD prolongs days, while the years of the wicked are shortened
The fear of the LORD shortens everyone’s days
The wicked’s years are lengthened by fearing the LORD
challenge.explanation: Verse 27 contrasts prolonged days with the shortened years of the wicked.
challenge.q: What connection is made between fearing the LORD and the end of the wicked?

answers: The righteous are stable and enduring, unlike the wicked who do not remain
The wicked are the stable foundation
The righteous depend only on wealth
challenge.explanation: Verses 25 and 30 emphasize the lasting security of the righteous and the passing away of the wicked.
challenge.q: What repeated idea appears in the passages about the whirlwind, the earth, and the righteous?

paragraphs.title: The Speech of the Righteous and the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom.”
easy.q: What does the mouth of the just bring forth?

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “the froward tongue shall be cut out.”
easy.q: What shall happen to the froward tongue?

easy.explanation: Verse 32 says, “The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable.”
easy.q: What do the lips of the righteous know?

answers: The just bring forth wisdom, while the froward tongue is cut out
The just tongue is cut out, while the froward tongue knows what is acceptable
medium.explanation: Verse 31 contrasts wisdom from the just with judgment upon the froward tongue.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the mouth of the just and the froward tongue?

answers: Speech that is perverse or twisted
medium.explanation: Froward speech is twisted, perverse, or contrary to what is right.

answers: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable
Only the wicked know what is acceptable
Acceptability is connected only with wealth
medium.explanation: Verse 32 directly says that the lips of the righteous know what is acceptable.
medium.q: What does the final verse teach about what is acceptable?

answers: It summarizes that righteous speech produces wisdom and acceptable things, while wicked speech is perverse
It teaches that every kind of speech is harmful
It focuses only on social rank
challenge.explanation: The final verses gather together the chapter’s contrast between beneficial and corrupt speech.
challenge.q: How does the ending expand the chapter’s earlier teaching about speech?

answers: They produce wisdom and recognize what is acceptable
challenge.explanation: The mouth of the just brings forth wisdom, and the lips of the righteous know what is acceptable.
challenge.q: What quality is shared by the words of the righteous in these final verses?

answers: It describes the removal or silencing of corrupt speech
It describes the joy of the righteous
challenge.explanation: The expression indicates a severe judgment against twisted and perverse speech.
challenge.q: Why is “cut out” a severe result for the froward tongue?
